utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, could you call the case please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, Douglas Stringer, Matthew Olmsted, Sarah Clanton, Thomas Laugel, and Morvarid Bagheri.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic and Christopher Gosnell. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we go into closed session -- is it closed session for the next witness? I'm not sure. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Before we go into closed session there is an oral ruling that we could deliver. On 17 June 2013 the Defence filed motion for reconsideration of the Trial Chamber's decision on 12 June to admit into evidence three newspaper articles through Witness GH-026. In its response, the Prosecution opposes the motion, arguing that the Defence has established no error on the part of the chamber in exercising its discretion to admitted exhibits. The Prosecution also argues that the newspaper articles are not unreliable as evidence. In its reply, the Defence reiterates its arguments that the newspaper articles are unreliable as evidence and should not be admitted. A Chamber has the discretion to reconsider a previous interlocutory decision in exceptional cases if a clear error of reasoning has been demonstrated or if it is necessary to do so to prevent an injustice. Particular circumstances justifying reconsideration include new facts or new arguments. The Trial Chamber decided to admit each of the three newspaper articles after the parties had had a full opportunity to make submissions on whether they should be admitted. In the motion, the Defence fails to demonstrate any error of reasoning on the part of the Chamber, nor has the Defence convinced the Chamber that it is necessary to reconsider the decision in order to prevent an injustice. The Trial Chamber recalls that the three newspaper articles are items of documentary hearsay evidence. The Chamber assures the parties - and especially the Defence - that, when deciding what weight to give to this evidence, it will take into account the circumstances under which the evidence arose and will consider the context and character of the evidence in question. In particular, the extent to which the witness was able to comment on the articles will be taken into account when the Chamber is considering the weight to attributed to these exhibits in light of the totality of the evidence on the record of the proceedings. For these reasons, the Defence is granted leave to file and a reply and the motion is denied. Madam Registrar, can we go into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, before we do that, the Prosecution had one very brief matter to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: However, I think we should go into private session for that, if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
